title: Anthropic will let Australia stress test dangerous new models
key_facts: Anthropic says it is finalising a deal that will allow Australia's AI Safety Institute to evaluate its powerful new frontier models.

In remarks prepared for a joint parliamentary hearing on Tuesday 6 Oct 2026, Anthropic general counsel Jeff Bleich said the company is finalising an agreement so the Institute can run its own independent evaluations, delivering on a memorandum of understanding signed with the government in April.

The Institute was set up last year with $29.9 million of federal funding; in April Anthropic had said it would run joint evaluations and share findings, and it now says it is allowing independent evaluations.

Anthropic is also pushing for a copyright arrangement that would let it train models in Australia; Bleich said it respects Australia's rejection of a wholesale text and data mining exemption and is discussing an alternative mechanism with the government.

Anthropic's head of safeguards said the company has not found any case of its agents interacting with Australian government systems in an unauthorised way, and that it would notify the Australian government within days of detecting any.

OpenAI took 84 days to notify the Australian government of the Medicare incident, according to Prime Minister Anthony Albanese; OpenAI chief strategy officer Jason Kwon apologised at the same inquiry on Tuesday.
Anthropic's interest in investing up to $15 billion in Australian data centres is well known; OpenAI has only a non-binding memorandum of understanding with NextDC.
quote_evidence: Anthropic says it is finalising a deal that will allow Australia’s AI Safety Institute to evaluate its powerful new frontier models as it continues to push for a copyright agreement allowing it to train those models in Australia.

“We are also delivering on the MOU we signed with the government in April by finalizing an agreement with the AI Safety Institute to enable it to run its own independent evaluations of our models,” Bleich wrote.
It took OpenAI 84 days to notify the Australian government of the Medicare incident, according to Prime Minister Anthony Albanese.
why_it_matters_hint: A government-funded institute would get to test an AI lab's strongest models independently, a step announced while the company seeks copyright and investment concessions; the deal is not yet signed.
event_date: Hearing Tuesday 6 Oct 2026 (Australia); the April 2026 memorandum of understanding is the earlier step
